note: NKX6-2-related SPAX8 manifests as an autosomal recessive spastic ataxia and hypomyelinating leukodystrophy spectrum whose key differentials include PLP1, GJC2, and POLR3 disorders.

evidence.text: NKX6-2-related disorder shows autosomal recessive inheritance and ranges from a severe neonatal presentation to a milder childhood-onset presentation dominated by slowly progressive complex spastic ataxia with pyramidal and cerebellar findings.

source.title: NKX6-2-Related Disorder - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
source.quote: NKX6-2-related disorder is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner. At conception, each sib of an affected individual has a 25% chance of being affected... At the milder end of the spectrum is normal achievement of early motor milestones in the first year of life followed by slowly progressive complex spastic ataxia

evidence.text: Affected individuals with bi-allelic NKX6-2 variants present with autosomal recessive early-onset spastic ataxia and hypomyelination, with milder cases having onset in childhood, very slow progression, and survival into adulthood.

source.title: Mutations in NKX6-2 cause progressive spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Affected members of two families had childhood onset disease with very slow progression. They are still alive in their 30s and 40s and show predominant ataxia and cerebellar atrophy features on imaging.
